content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} state sales tax on a car, with no credit for tax paid in another state. Registration and title fees are small; yearly county taxes depend on the vehicle's value.

howItWorks.text: The state rate is {stateRate} of the net price after dealer discounts and your trade-in. Manufacturer rebates do not lower it.
Tax paid to another state is not credited against the Mississippi tax when you register the vehicle.
Privilege and ad valorem taxes are charged on top and vary by the vehicle's value and where you live. Your county tax collector gives the total.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in Mississippi?
faq.text: Yes, the tax is figured on the net price after dealer discounts and trade-ins.

faq.q: Is tax paid in another state credited?
faq.text: No, the department says it is not credited toward the Mississippi tax.
